entry.title: CrossDistill: Balancing Quality and Diversity
entry.content:
CrossDistill is a trajectory-level hybrid few-step distillation method designed to balance generation quality and diversity. It splits sampling at a crossover point, preserving modes at high noise and matching distributions at low noise.

entry.title: RoLA: Rotary-Positioned Low-Rank Linear Attention
entry.content:
RoLA introduces a rotary-positioned low-rank linear attention branch for efficient Diffusion Transformers. The design combines low-rank linear attention with rotary positional information for efficient visual generation.

entry.title: RoPeSLR: Sparse-Low-Rank Attention for Diffusion Transformers

link.title: RoPeSLR: Sparse-Low-Rank Attention for Diffusion Transformers

entry.content:
RoPeSLR is a 3D RoPE-driven sparse-low-rank attention framework for efficient Diffusion Transformers. It decouples attention into sparse and low-rank components while retaining positional structure for visual generation.

entry.title: CR-Net: Cross-Layer Low-Rank Structure
entry.content:
CR-Net explores cross-layer low-rank structure to scale parameter-efficient large language model training. The method shares and organizes low-rank information across layers rather than treating every layer independently.

The work was accepted by ICLR 2026.

entry.title: Mixture of Distributions Matters
entry.content:
Long-sequence video generation is constrained by the quadratic cost of self-attention. Mixture of Distributions Matters studies dynamic sparse attention for efficient video Diffusion Transformers and adapts attention computation to the heterogeneous distributions encountered during generation.

The work was accepted by ICML 2026.

  • arXiv
  • Code
  • Project page
entry.summary: Dynamic sparse attention for efficient video Diffusion Transformers.

entry.title: MISA: Memory-Efficient LLM Optimization
entry.content:
MISA is a memory-efficient optimization method for large language models. It uses module-wise importance sampling to reduce the memory demands of pre-training and fine-tuning while retaining the optimization signal from selected modules.

The work was accepted by NeurIPS 2025.
